chunks: And regarding the heel, when it is bruised and bandaged without a fracture or defect, [the compensation is] one-third of the wergild of the leg, being three hundred and thirty-three dinars and one-third of a dinar.
ai.seo_question: What is the compensation for a bruised heel without fracture in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* details the specific *diyah* (blood money) for a bruised heel (*al-kab*) that heals without fracture or defect, establishing it as one-third of the full leg wergild. The precise valuation of 333 and one-third dinars reflects the early Islamic monetary system and the jurisprudential rigor of the Ahl al-Bayt in quantifying bodily injuries. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on precise legal categorization of physical harm, distinguishing between temporary injury and permanent impairment.
